questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests hands-on ability to apply Kubernetes NetworkPolicy for multi-namespace isolation and least privilege, including default-deny and per-port allow rules, plus practical troubleshooting steps.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy basics
- namespaceSelector and podSelector
- Ingress vs Egress rules and reciprocity
- Troubleshooting pod reachability with test pods

## Code Example
```yaml
# api-prod-default-deny
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-prod-default-deny
  namespace: api-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-prod
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
```

```yaml
# api-prod-to-logging (allow egress to logging)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-prod-to-logging
  namespace: api-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-prod
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: logging
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

```yaml
# logging-accept-api-prod (allow ingress from api-prod to logging)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: logging-accept-api-prod
  namespace: logging
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: logging
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: api-prod
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

```yaml
# api-prod-to-db (allow egress to db-prod on 5432)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-prod-to-db
  namespace: api-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-prod
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: db-prod
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
```

```yaml
# db-accept-api-prod (allow ingress from api-prod to db)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: db-accept-api-prod
  namespace: db-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: api-prod
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you verify no other cross-namespace traffic is allowed after policies apply?
- How would you roll back if a required path is blocked by policy?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This question evaluates a candidate's ability to plan and execute certificate rotation in a live Kubernetes cluster with minimal or no downtime. It assesses understanding of TLS certificate management, control plane high availability, and operational safety procedures.

## Key Concepts
- TLS certificate rotation in Kubernetes
- Rolling control-plane updates
- etcd TLS configuration
- kubeconfig refresh and client validation
- Safe rollback strategies and backups

## Code Example
```bash
# 1. Backup existing certificates
cp -r /etc/kubernetes/pki /etc/kubernetes/pki.bak
cp -r /etc/etcd/pki /etc/etcd/pki.bak

# 2. Generate new CA (using kubeadm)
kubeadm init phase certs ca --cert-dir /etc/kubernetes/pki

# 3. Generate new kube-apiserver certificate
kubeadm init phase certs apiserver --cert-dir /etc/kubernetes/pki

# 4. Generate new etcd CA and certificates
kubeadm init phase certs etcd-ca --cert-dir /etc/etcd/pki
kubeadm init phase certs etcd-server --cert-dir /etc/etcd/pki

# 5. Restart kubelet to pick up new certificates
systemctl restart kubelet

# 6. Verify certificates
openssl x509 -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt -noout -dates
openssl x509 -in /etc/etcd/pki/server.crt -noout -dates
```

## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical knowledge of securing workloads via Pod Security Standards and admission controls, plus concrete remediation steps.

## Key Concepts
- Pod Security Standards (restricted)
- Pod securityContext and container securityContext
- MutatingAdmissionWebhook implications
- Patching deployments and verifying compliance

## Code Example
```yaml
# Patch example to enforce container securityContext on a deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

- How would you rollback if a legitimate app requires root privileges?

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:

spec:

          exec:
            command: ["pg_isready"]

```
